subject: Inference performance MOP and acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@fastfin.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@fastfin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inference performance MOP and acceptance criteria

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for the time today. I wanted to capture a short Mutual Action Plan (MOP) and the acceptance criteria we discussed so the whole team is aligned. Below is a concise summary from our call and the immediate next steps.

Key pain points you shared
- Unpredictable p95 tail latency on text-generation endpoints during bursts (particularly when your UI does simultaneous chat streams).
- First-token delay for streaming responses — product team wants near-instant streaming to preserve perceived real-time UX.
- Cost spikes under concurrency; current provider scales vertically and you get high per-token cost at peak.
- Cold-start variability when a model scales up from zero.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Triton + K8s serving for model endpoints (mixed-instance GPU fleet, some V100s, one experimental H100 node).
- API gateway with baked-in rate limits and per-customer throttles (Nginx).
- Edge web clients using long-lived streams for chat.

Success criteria (acceptance) — proposed
1) p95 latency (all tokens) <= 300 ms for 256-token requests at steady state; p99 < 700 ms.
2) Streaming first-token latency (time-to-first-byte) < 150 ms 95% of the time for the chat UX.
3) Sustained concurrent active requests: support 200 concurrent generation sessions with acceptable degradation (p95 SLA target met).
4) No more than 20% cost increase vs baseline at the expected 2x traffic burst — we will include batching/kv-cache suggestions to control unit economics.

Proposed MOP (next 3 weeks)
- Week 1: Redwood runs a short benchmark against a representative model (your 256-token prompt set) and shares a benchmark-summary CSV (attached). We’ll request a short IP allowlist for our test harness.
- Week 2: Joint streaming demo — we’ll instrument first-byte timings and show client-side integration patterns that minimize friction. Schedule: 30-min demo (link below).
- Week 3: Pilot proposal with a small Dedicated pool (or hosted with reserved capacity) and success metrics dashboard access for your SREs.

Immediate asks from FastFin
- Provide a short prompt corpus (10 prompts representative of peak queries) and a list of endpoints you consider high priority.
- Security & procurement contact so we can start the SOC2 questionnaire and IP allowlist.

Attachments: FastFin-mop-v1.pdf (MOP outline) and benchmark-summary-256tokens.csv (initial run).

If this looks right I’ll: 1) send a calendar invite for the demo, 2) open the pilot proposal doc, and 3) kick off the benchmark run.

Thanks —

Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Redwood Inference — High-performance inference for production LLMs
From: Samir Khan <samir@fastfin.com>

Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference performance MOP and acceptance criteria

Monica — thanks for the clear write-up. Quick confirmations and one tweak from our side:

- The p95 target looks reasonable for steady state. For streaming-first-byte, we really need < 120 ms at 95% for our mobile clients — that number is a hard UX requirement. Can Redwood demonstrate that in the demo?
- Our current fleet mixes GPUs; we will share the node labels and a small corpus by EOD so your benchmark reflects our real traffic.
- Cold-starts are our biggest pain during scale-ups. Anything you can instrument to show cold-start percentiles in the benchmark will be valuable.

Next actions on our side: I’ll share the prompt corpus and the procurement contact (procure@fastfin.com). Elena will follow up on security questionnaire items and provide the allowlist IPs.

On the demo, please propose two times next week — mornings PST work best for our team.

—Samir
VP Product, FastFin
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Samir Khan <samir@fastfin.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@fastfin.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference performance MOP and acceptance criteria

Looping in a couple of operational notes from our infra team that will help set expectations for the benchmark:

- Benchmarks will include both steady-state and burst profiles. For cold-starts, we will run a scale-from-zero experiment and report the 95/99 cold-start latency numbers.
- For streaming-first-byte, we’ll test both direct streaming and a websocket-proxied configuration (some customers see lower first-byte using a persistent process).
- If FastFin prefers deterministic tail latency we recommend we include a small dedicated pool in the pilot — that’s where the most predictable p95 behavior comes from. I’ll prepare an ops-runbook stub to attach to the pilot proposal.

Ben
Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@fastfin.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@fastfin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference performance MOP and acceptance criteria

Thanks Samir — that’s helpful. I booked two slots on Calendly and included both in the HubSpot activity: 09:00 PDT and 16:00 PDT on Tue/Thu next week. Please pick the one that works and I’ll send calendar invites.

Summary of agreed next steps (short):
- FastFin: share prompt corpus + procurement contact + allowlist IPs (Samir / Elena) — by EOD Fri.
- Redwood: run benchmark (include cold-start profile) + share benchmark CSV and ops runbook + 30-min streaming demo.
- Both: review pilot proposal and finalize success KPIs (we’ll pre-fill with the acceptance criteria above).

I’ll follow up with the MOP PDF updated for Samir’s 120 ms streaming-first-byte ask and the pilot proposal this afternoon.

Monica
